Tom — thanks for sending this over and for attaching the questionnaire. Long story short: we support both termination modes but recommend a single responsibility matrix for production to avoid split-TLS complexity.

Summary of recommended approach for acme-prod-vpc:
- Primary: Terminate at the customer-managed NLB/ALB inside the VPC when you require customer KMS control and mTLS to your backends. This gives you full control of certs and private key material.
- Alternative (Redwood-managed): Terminate at Redwood edge if you want simplified rollouts and centralized certificate rotation; Redwood will accept SANs for private FQDNs and rotate via our KMS. This is our fallback for low-trust test tenants.

DNS proofing: we prefer a DNS TXT proving flow for private zones (TXT entry under _redwood-proof.<hostname>) because HTTP-01 is fragile inside private networks. If you cannot write TXT records, we can accept an offline CSR + signed proof workflow.

I'll attach an accountability matrix (who does what) and a short CSR sample for the team. Can Neha and Karthik confirm operational constraints?

1) Confirm delegation method (TXT vs CSR) by EOD Fri.
2) If TXT chosen: provide a TTL and the zone owner contact so we can verify.
3) If you want Redwood-managed termination: provide KMS access model or sign an escrow agreement.

Hi all — quick technical clarifications from infra:
- SNI: if you terminate at Redwood edge, we rely on SNI to route to the correct tenant. For private FQDNs ensure the client includes SNI (most ACME clients and SDKs do).
- mTLS: If Acme wants client-auth at the edge we support mutual TLS, but the client certs must be provided by Acme (we can host a CRL or OCSP responder).
- Wildcard certs: supported but we prefer explicit SAN lists for private zones to avoid wildcard leakage.
- TXT proof: we will look for a single random token under _redwood-proof.<target>.example.internal and verify it. TTL >= 300s is fine.

Operational ask: if you choose customer-side termination, we will still need a short-lived CSR (PEM) that includes the required SANs so our routing mesh can validate the origin cert (not to hold private keys).

Link to internal runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Rt-private-tls-playbook (read-only for partners with link).

Neha
